newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-TRINIDAD PM SAYS INDISCIPLINE BEHIND DEBACLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TRINIDAD PM SAYS INDISCIPLINE BEHIND DEBACLE.

text.p: The Prime Minister of Trinidad and Tobago, on a tour of India, on Wednesday cited poor leadership and a lack of discipline for West Indies's cricket debacle against Australia this week.

"The team is going through a bad patch. It is because of a combination of factors like leadership and discipline," Basdeo Panday told Reuters after a business luncheon at Bangalore during a two-week visit to India.

But he said star Trinidadian batsman Brian Lara should not be burdened with the captaincy of the side. "Captaincy brings in a lot of pressure. I really don't know whether it will be right for Lara to take over captaincy."
Australia took a 3-1 lead over the West Indies on Monday by winning their fourth test in the five-match series.

The Windies, once the game's cavalier leaders but now going through a crisis, suffered their biggest test match loss to Australia since the 1930-31 series as they lost by an innings and 183 runs at Adelaide.
This was their third biggest all-time defeat and their worst since losing to England at the Oval in 1957 by an innings and 237 runs.
Panday said he hoped the team would extricate itself from the abyss they had fallen into.
"Definitely they are going through a rut, but I am sure they will come out of it. When you are down the only way is to climb up," he added.

Cricket, a passion with West Indians in the past, has taken a back seat in recent years to other sports that are faster, provide more instant excitement and, most importantly, finish in under three hours.
